Run Data-Driven cIPMA with Causal Discovery

Source: R/discovery_cipma.R
discovery_cipma.Rd

This function performs causal discovery using constraint-based, score-based, or hybrid algorithms to learn the structural model from data, then runs cIPMA on the discovered structure. This exploratory approach is useful when theoretical guidance is limited or when researchers want to compare theory-driven and data-driven models.

Usage

discovery_cipma(
  data,
  measurement_model,
  target_construct,
  scales,
  target_level = 85,
  nca_rep = NULL,
  pi = 1,
  B = 1999L,
  algorithm = "hc",
  blacklist = NULL,
  whitelist = NULL,
  algorithm.args = list(),
  nboot = 1000
)

Arguments

data

The raw data frame containing indicator variables.

measurement_model

A seminr measurement model object (defined with constructs()).

target_construct

String. The name of the dependent variable for cIPMA.

scales

A named list of theoretical min/max for each indicator.

target_level

Numeric. Desired target construct level (0-100). Default is 85.

nca_rep

Deprecated. Number of permutations; use B.

pi

Tolerance of the bottleneck, passed to cipma. Default 1.

B

Number of permutations of the significance test, passed to cipma. Default 1999.

algorithm

Character. Causal discovery algorithm. Options:

  • Score-based: "hc" (default), "tabu"

  • Constraint-based: "pc", "gs", "iamb", "fast.iamb", "inter.iamb", "mmpc", "hpc"

  • Hybrid: "mmhc", "h2pc", "rsmax2"

blacklist

Optional. A data frame with columns 'from' and 'to' specifying forbidden arcs (e.g., based on temporal ordering or theory).

whitelist

Optional. A data frame with columns 'from' and 'to' specifying required arcs (e.g., well-established theoretical relationships).

algorithm.args

Optional. A list of additional arguments to pass to the bnlearn algorithm (e.g., list(restart = 10) for hc, list(alpha = 0.01) for constraint-based algorithms).

nboot

Integer. Number of bootstrap samples for PLS-SEM. Default 1000. Use lower values (e.g., 500) for faster exploratory runs.

Value

A cipma object with additional elements:

  • learned_graph: The bnlearn network object

  • discovered_arcs: Data frame of discovered relationships

  • algorithm: The algorithm used for discovery

Details

This function implements the causal discovery approach for PLS-SEM as discussed by Richter et al. (2020), who argue that combining causal discovery algorithms with PLS-SEM can be valuable for:

  • Exploratory research where theory is underdeveloped

  • Model comparison (theory-driven vs. data-driven)

  • Identifying potentially missing paths in existing models

  • Cross-validation of theoretical assumptions

The function uses proxy scores (standardized mean of indicators) for structure learning, which is consistent with the composite-based nature of PLS-SEM. After structure learning, proper PLS-SEM estimation is performed on the original indicators.

Available Algorithms

Score-based (fast)

  • "hc": Hill-Climbing (default) - greedy search, fastest

  • "tabu": Tabu Search - avoids local optima

Constraint-based

  • "pc": PC algorithm (stable version)

  • "gs": Grow-Shrink

  • "iamb": Incremental Association Markov Blanket

  • "fast.iamb": Fast IAMB

  • "inter.iamb": Interleaved IAMB

  • "mmpc": Max-Min Parents and Children

  • "hpc": Hybrid Parents and Children

Hybrid (recommended for robustness)

  • "mmhc": Max-Min Hill-Climbing

  • "h2pc": Hybrid HPC

  • "rsmax2": General 2-phase Restricted Maximization

Runtime Note

The main computational cost comes from PLS-SEM bootstrapping (Step 4), not structure learning. Consider reducing nboot (e.g., 500) for initial exploration, then increase for final results.

Caution

Results from causal discovery should be interpreted as exploratory hypotheses requiring theoretical justification and replication. The discovered structure represents statistical associations that may reflect causal relationships but cannot establish causality from observational data alone.

References

Richter, N. F., Schubring, S., Hauff, S., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2020). When predictors of outcomes are necessary: Guidelines for the combined use of PLS-SEM and NCA. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 120(12), 2243-2267.

Scutari, M. (2010). Learning Bayesian Networks with the bnlearn R Package. Journal of Statistical Software, 35(3), 1-22.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example with whitelist (required arcs) and blacklist (forbidden arcs)

# Whitelist: Theory strongly supports these paths
whitelist <- data.frame(
  from = c("Quality", "Satisfaction"),
  to = c("Satisfaction", "Loyalty")
)

# Blacklist: These paths are theoretically impossible
blacklist <- data.frame(
  from = c("Loyalty", "Loyalty"),
  to = c("Quality", "Satisfaction")
)

# Run with hybrid algorithm (recommended)
result <- discovery_cipma(
  data = survey_data,
  measurement_model = mm,
  target_construct = "Loyalty",
  scales = scales,
  algorithm = "mmhc",
  whitelist = whitelist,
  blacklist = blacklist,
  nboot = 500  # Lower for faster exploration
)

# View discovered structure
print(result$discovered_arcs)
} # }
